lines: +The old proxy built prompts by appending one rendered message at a time to a single per-episode buffer. That assumes the chat template is concatenative and history never changes — false for the GLM agent template (older reasoning/user text is rewritten as the conversation grows) and for Terminus-2 summarization (history is replaced, unwound, and branched for summary/questions/answers). Hence prompts diverged from SGLang and eventually exceeded the context length. The proxy now re-renders every request the way SGLang's chat endpoint does (protocol-level message/tool normalization, content-part handling, last-assistant rule, per-request `chat_template_kwargs`/`reasoning_effort`, stringified tool-call arguments parsed back to objects), then splices in earlier engine token ids where the new rendered text starts with an earlier prompt/generation of the same agent, so sampled tokens are not re-tokenized. Samples are only merged across turns where the next prompt literally starts with the previous prompt+generation ids; otherwise a turn starts a new row, so every trained token keeps its sampled context.

+Agents were keyed by the episode URL, so explorers were folded into the main agent. Sessions are now keyed by the agent's own session id (`X-Session-ID` / body `session_id`), explorers get their own samples, and `finish` on the episode returns every agent's rows. Engine `abort` results were reported to agents as finished `stop` answers and trained, as were generations for requests clients had abandoned. Aborts now return 503 (an engine-side 4xx in the abort reason is passed through), client disconnects/duplicates abort the engine request by `rid`, and nothing undelivered is recorded. Because a gateway can also drop a response after the proxy sent it, the latest generation is tentative: an identical re-send replaces it, a different next request confirms it. Output parsing now follows SGLang's reasoning-detector semantics and only parses tool calls when the request carries tools. `check_samples.py` passed throughout because the fake engine's log-probs hash whatever prompt the proxy actually sent — internally consistent samples say nothing about prompt fidelity, delivery, or explorers.

+Verification: unit tests in `terminal_rl/tests/` pass. Full replay (fake engine, `--abort-rate 0.05`): GLM — all 1618 engine prompts match SGLang's rendering exactly, 1412 samples over 76 agents/40 episodes, 0 logprob mismatches; Qwen — all 646 prompt texts match (92 prompts deliberately reuse sampled ids instead of a re-tokenization), 409 trained turns in 110 samples, 0 logprob mismatches, no aborted or undelivered generation trained in either replay. Live run `20261025-112201` (`/opt/live/run.sh`) completed: 184 requests through the gateway (27 responses dropped after sending, 8 given up, 12 generations aborted by 4 weight updates), 36 rows from `finish` over 8 episodes.
